exposure: Diagnosis methods (Nitrazine test, ferning, commercial tests like PAMG-1/IGFBP-1, ultrasonography)
Management strategies (antenatal corticosteroids, magnesium sulphate, antibiotic treatment, tocolysis, bed rest, hospital/home management, cervical cerclage, timing of delivery)
outcome: Short- and long-term severe neonatal morbidity (periventricular leukomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, retinopathy of prematurity, adverse neurodevelopment outcomes)
Recurrence risk of PPROM in future pregnancies
cohort: The guidelines are targeted at all patients experiencing preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) before 37 weeks gestation.
finding: The primary finding is a comprehensive set of evidence-based guidelines for the diagnosis and management of preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) in Canadian patients.
mod_finding: The guideline discusses the timing and method of delivery, recommending induction of labour for Group B Streptococcus colonization in late-preterm PPROM, but does not provide specific comparative findings on different birth modes.
gest_age: <37 weeks gestation (general guidelines), <34 weeks gestation (expectant management), 34^0 to 36^6 weeks gestation (late-preterm period considerations)
